topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Dynamic Changes

sections.title: Introduction: Beyond the Static Slope
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure dynamic change, not static slopes.
Average speed hides the cheetah's instant velocity.
Watch the speedometer at one exact millisecond.
Derivatives capture this instantaneous sensitivity perfectly.
Position data transforms into vital movement insights.
animations: Draw a curve in #FFD700 to represent a position graph.
Animate a moving point (cheetah) along the curve in #FF0000.
Show a secant line between two points shrinking as they converge.
Fade in a tangent line in #00FF00 at the target point.
Highlight the final slope value with a glowing pulse effect.

sections.title: The Visual Mechanism: The Shrinking Secant
lecture_lines: A secant connects two points on the curve.
Zoom in as the distance shrinks toward zero.
The line tilts, tracking the roller coaster.
It snaps perfectly into the tangent line.
This limit defines the instantaneous derivative.
animations: Plot a curve in #FFD700 representing a roller coaster path.
Draw a secant line in #00FFFF connecting two distant points on the curve.
Animate one point moving closer to the other point along the curve.
Show the secant line rotating and converging toward the tangent line.
Lock the line as the tangent in #00FF00 when distance is zero.

sections.title: Derivative as a Transformation Map
lecture_lines: Derivatives act as a function-to-function machine.
Input temperature; output the rate of change.
It reveals how fast the room heats.
animations: Show a temperature function graph in #FFD700.
Animate a derivative machine icon transforming input into output.
Display output as a dynamic rate-of-change graph in #FF00FF.
Change color of the derivative machine to #FFFFFF to show active transformation.
Overlay text 'Rate of Change' next to the second graph.

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation: The Slope Field
lecture_lines: Visualize derivatives as a field of arrows.
Each arrow shows flow at that coordinate.
Ocean currents map the function's directionality.
animations: Draw a grid of points on the screen.
Generate a vector field of arrows in #00FFFF showing flow directions.
Animate a particle path flowing through the vector field.
Highlight one arrow in #FFFFFF as the particle passes.
Dim the background grid to emphasize the flow field.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
lecture_lines: Derivatives reveal the DNA of dynamic change.
We transformed static slopes into system flow.
Now, we are prepared for reverse integration.
animations: Show key concepts from previous sections floating on screen.
Merge elements into a single 'Dynamic Change' icon in center.
Animate the icon pulsing in #FFFFFF.
Fade out all elements except the central icon.
Display text 'Ready for Integration' on screen.
